question: Can a large, slow ensemble be compressed into a small, fast model with little loss in accuracy?
hypothesis: A neural net trained on enough ensemble-labeled pseudo data will approximate the ensemble's function and not overfit.
contributions: Model compression: train a compact neural net on ensemble-labeled pseudo data
MUNGE, a nearest-neighbour swap/perturb method for synthetic data
Experiments on eight problems showing near-ensemble accuracy at about 1000x smaller and faster

method.summary: Ensemble selection models are built from 4000 training points and a 1000-point validation set. Pseudo data is generated from the training set (RANDOM, NBE or MUNGE), labeled by the ensemble, and a neural net with 1 to 256 hidden units is trained on it (early stopping on the validation set). RMSE is measured on large test sets.

metrics.name: RMSE
metrics.definition: root-mean-squared error of model predictions to binary 0/1 targets on large independent test sets

metrics.name: improvement ratio
metrics.definition: (best ANN - mimic net) / (best ANN - ensemble); 1.0 means equal to ensemble

limits: Ensemble size (number of base models) and MUNGE p, s values are not stated; no optimizer, learning rate or epochs for the net.
Only eight binary tabular problems with 4000 training points; no deep teachers, no multiclass.
ADULT (high-arity nominal attributes) is not compressed well; cause unresolved (neural nets or MUNGE).
MUNGE is less sample efficient than real unlabeled data (2-8x on COVTYPE).
Compression can cost more than building the original ensemble (labeling and training); justified only for constrained or high-volume deployment.
Speed numbers depend on implementation; authors say some could improve 10x or more.

code.snippet: MUNGE(T,k,p,s): repeat k times: for each e in T' find closest e'; per attribute a: if continuous, with prob p set e_a~N(e'_a,sd), e'_a~N(e_a,sd), sd=|e_a-e'_a|/s; else with prob p swap values of a between e and e'; append T' to D
